vulnerability.name: CVE-2026-84304
vulnerability.description: gRPC-go: heap memory exhaustion via HTTP/2 DATA frame fragmentation

statements.impact_statement: The vulnerable grpc-go is vendored inside the upstream Trivy release binary the worker image carries (/usr/local/bin/trivy, pinned by TRIVY_VERSION in Containerfile.worker), not in any BatleHub code. The worker only ever runs it as a client against the Trivy server the chart deploys (crates/adapters/src/scanners/trivy.rs runs `trivy ... --server <endpoint>`); nothing in the image terminates an HTTP/2 connection of its own, so no attacker-controlled peer can send it the fragmented DATA frames the advisory describes.
statements.action_statement: Bump TRIVY_VERSION to the first Trivy release whose go.mod carries grpc-go >= 1.83.1, and delete this statement together with its .trivyignore.yaml entry.

vulnerability.name: CVE-2026-84445
vulnerability.description: gRPC-go: xDS routing interceptor panics on a request with neither :authority nor Host

statements.impact_statement: The vulnerable path is a server built with xds.NewGRPCServer(), and the Trivy binary in the worker image never builds one — it is invoked as a client, and Trivy's own server mode is plain gRPC rather than xDS, so the xDS routing interceptor the advisory describes is never installed. Nothing in the worker image listens on a port.
statements.action_statement: Bump TRIVY_VERSION to the first Trivy release whose go.mod carries grpc-go >= 1.82.2, and delete this statement together with its .trivyignore.yaml entry.

vulnerability.name: CVE-2026-78667
vulnerability.description: Go net/http: CPU exhaustion via crafted HTTP Range headers in FileServer, ServeContent and ServeFile

statements.impact_statement: The vulnerable Go standard library is compiled into the upstream Trivy release binary the worker image carries (/usr/local/bin/trivy, pinned by TRIVY_VERSION in Containerfile.worker), not into any BatleHub code. The worker only runs it as a scanning client (crates/adapters/src/scanners/trivy.rs runs `trivy rootfs|fs ... [--server <endpoint>]`), and nothing in the image listens. The advisory's path is net/http's file serving, which a client never enters: no request reaches this binary to carry a Range header.
statements.action_statement: Bump TRIVY_VERSION to the first Trivy release built with Go >= 1.26.9 or >= 1.27.2, and delete this statement together with its .trivyignore.yaml entry.

vulnerability.name: CVE-2026-97031
vulnerability.description: Go crypto/tls: server memory exhaustion via multiple ECH outer extension references

statements.impact_statement: The vulnerable Go standard library is compiled into the upstream Trivy release binary the worker image carries (/usr/local/bin/trivy, pinned by TRIVY_VERSION in Containerfile.worker), not into any BatleHub code. The worker only runs it as a scanning client (crates/adapters/src/scanners/trivy.rs runs `trivy rootfs|fs ... [--server <endpoint>]`), and nothing in the image listens. The advisory's path is a TLS server parsing a ClientHello; this binary only ever dials out, so it is never the server a crafted ClientHello would reach.
statements.action_statement: Bump TRIVY_VERSION to the first Trivy release built with Go >= 1.26.9 or >= 1.27.2, and delete this statement together with its .trivyignore.yaml entry.
